collection.name: Базові медичні дисципліни
collection.description: Ситуаційні задачі у форматі Кроку 1 англійською

questions.text: After removal of an impacted lower third molar, a patient has lost general sensation in the mucosa of the anterior two-thirds of the tongue on the same side. Taste is preserved. Which nerve has most likely been injured?
questions.explanation: General sensation of the anterior two-thirds of the tongue is carried by the lingual nerve (a branch of the mandibular nerve); taste is carried by the chorda tympani.

questions.text: Before extraction of a lower molar, the dentist performs an inferior alveolar nerve block. Through which opening does the inferior alveolar nerve enter the mandibular canal?
questions.explanation: The inferior alveolar nerve enters the mandibular canal through the mandibular foramen on the medial surface of the ramus.

questions.text: Which muscle is mainly responsible for protrusion of the mandible?
options: Anterior belly of the digastric muscle
questions.explanation: Bilateral contraction of the lateral pterygoid muscles pulls the condyles and discs forward, protruding the mandible.

questions.text: After surgery on the parotid gland, a patient cannot close the eye on the operated side, and the corner of the mouth droops. Which nerve has been damaged?
questions.explanation: The facial nerve passes through the parotid gland and supplies the muscles of facial expression, including the orbicularis oculi.

questions.text: The duct of the parotid gland opens into the oral vestibule opposite which tooth?
questions.explanation: The parotid (Stensen's) duct pierces the buccinator and opens on a papilla opposite the upper second molar.

questions.text: Motor innervation of the muscles of mastication is provided by which nerve?
questions.explanation: All muscles of mastication are supplied by motor branches of the mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve (V3).

questions.text: When a patient protrudes the tongue, it deviates to the right. Damage to which nerve is the most likely cause?
questions.explanation: With a hypoglossal nerve lesion, the intact genioglossus pushes the tongue toward the paralysed side.

questions.text: Where does the duct of the submandibular gland open?
options: In the vestibule opposite the upper second molar
At the foramen caecum of the tongue
On the dorsum of the tongue
questions.explanation: The submandibular (Wharton's) duct opens on the sublingual caruncle at the base of the lingual frenulum.

questions.text: The articular disc of the temporomandibular joint divides the joint cavity into how many compartments?
questions.explanation: The disc separates the TMJ into an upper and a lower joint cavity.

questions.text: The teeth of the lower jaw receive arterial blood mainly from which artery?
questions.explanation: The inferior alveolar artery, a branch of the maxillary artery, runs in the mandibular canal and supplies the lower teeth.

questions.text: To anaesthetize the greater palatine nerve, the needle is directed to the greater palatine foramen. Where is this foramen usually located?
options: Medial to the upper second or third molar
On the lateral surface of the maxillary tuberosity
questions.explanation: The greater palatine foramen lies in the posterior hard palate, usually medial to the second or third maxillary molar.

questions.text: Which nerve carries taste sensation from the posterior one-third of the tongue?
questions.explanation: Both taste and general sensation of the posterior third of the tongue are carried by the glossopharyngeal nerve.

questions.text: During a mental nerve block, the dentist palpates the mental foramen. Where is it most commonly located in adults?
options: At the angle of the mandible
questions.explanation: In most adults the mental foramen lies below the apex of the second premolar or between the premolars.

questions.text: Which cells produce the organic matrix of enamel?
questions.explanation: Enamel is secreted by ameloblasts, which differentiate from the inner enamel epithelium.

questions.text: Odontoblasts, which form dentin, differentiate from cells of which structure?
questions.explanation: Odontoblasts arise from the ectomesenchyme of the dental papilla, which also gives rise to the pulp.

questions.text: Cementum, the periodontal ligament and alveolar bone proper develop from which structure?
questions.explanation: The dental follicle (dental sac) gives rise to the supporting tissues of the tooth.

questions.text: Which dental tissue cannot regenerate after the tooth has erupted, because the cells that formed it are lost?
questions.explanation: Ameloblasts are lost after eruption, so enamel cannot be repaired biologically.

questions.text: What is the basic structural unit of enamel?
questions.explanation: Enamel consists of tightly packed hydroxyapatite crystals organized into enamel rods (prisms).

questions.text: On a ground section of a tooth, brownish incremental lines are seen in the enamel. They reflect the rhythmic formation of enamel. What are these lines called?
questions.explanation: Striae of Retzius are incremental growth lines of enamel; lines of von Ebner and Owen are found in dentin.

questions.text: Epithelial rests of Malassez found in the periodontal ligament are remnants of which structure?
questions.explanation: Hertwig's root sheath breaks up after root formation, leaving the epithelial rests of Malassez.

questions.text: What type of epithelium covers the hard palate and the attached gingiva?
questions.explanation: Masticatory mucosa (hard palate, attached gingiva) is covered by keratinized or parakeratinized stratified squamous epithelium.

questions.text: Which lingual papillae are the most numerous and do not contain taste buds?
questions.explanation: Filiform papillae have a mechanical function and lack taste buds.

questions.text: A newborn has a cleft of the upper lip. Failure of fusion of which embryonic structures causes this defect?
options: Medial nasal process and maxillary process
Lateral nasal process and maxillary process
questions.explanation: The upper lip forms when the medial nasal processes fuse with the maxillary processes.

questions.text: Dentinal tubules contain the cytoplasmic processes of which cells?
questions.explanation: Each dentinal tubule contains an odontoblast process (Tomes' fibre).

questions.text: At which stage of tooth development do ameloblasts and odontoblasts differentiate?
questions.explanation: Histodifferentiation of ameloblasts and odontoblasts takes place at the bell stage.

questions.text: Which major salivary gland in adults is composed almost exclusively of serous acini?
questions.explanation: The parotid is a purely serous gland; the submandibular is mixed, and the sublingual is mainly mucous.

questions.text: Stimulation of which nerve fibres produces a large volume of watery saliva rich in water and electrolytes?
options: Sensory fibres of the trigeminal nerve
questions.explanation: Parasympathetic stimulation causes abundant watery saliva; sympathetic stimulation produces a small amount of viscous saliva.

questions.text: What is the normal pH range of mixed saliva?
questions.explanation: Resting saliva is slightly acidic to neutral, approximately pH 6.2–7.4.

questions.text: Which salivary enzyme starts the digestion of starch in the oral cavity?
questions.explanation: Salivary alpha-amylase (ptyalin) breaks down starch into smaller carbohydrates.

questions.text: Below which approximate pH value does dental enamel (hydroxyapatite) begin to dissolve?
questions.explanation: The critical pH for hydroxyapatite is about 5.5; fluorapatite is more resistant (about 4.5).

questions.text: Where is the swallowing centre located?
questions.explanation: The swallowing (deglutition) centre is located in the medulla oblongata.

questions.text: Which substance is responsible for the umami taste?
questions.explanation: Umami taste is triggered by glutamate; sodium ions give salty taste and hydrogen ions sour taste.

questions.text: Which hormone increases the level of calcium in the blood by stimulating bone resorption by osteoclasts?
questions.explanation: Parathyroid hormone raises blood calcium; calcitonin lowers it.

questions.text: Salivary lysozyme protects the oral cavity by which mechanism?
options: It hydrolyses the peptidoglycan of bacterial cell walls
It binds iron needed by bacteria
It neutralizes acids in dental plaque
questions.explanation: Lysozyme breaks the bonds in peptidoglycan, damaging the cell walls of bacteria, mainly Gram-positive ones.

questions.text: What is the approximate daily volume of saliva secreted by a healthy adult?
questions.explanation: A healthy adult produces roughly 0.5 to 1.5 litres of saliva per day.

questions.text: What kind of saliva is produced when the sympathetic nervous system stimulates the salivary glands?
options: A small amount of viscous saliva rich in proteins
A large amount of watery saliva
Saliva with a very low pH
questions.explanation: Sympathetic stimulation produces scanty, thick saliva rich in mucins and other proteins.

questions.text: Which hormone increases the absorption of calcium in the small intestine?
questions.explanation: Calcitriol (active vitamin D) stimulates intestinal absorption of calcium and phosphate.

questions.text: Pain from the dental pulp is conducted mainly by which nerve fibres?
questions.explanation: Sharp pulpal pain is carried by A-delta fibres and dull, throbbing pain by unmyelinated C fibres.

questions.text: What is the main mineral component of tooth enamel?
questions.explanation: About 96% of enamel by weight is mineral, mainly hydroxyapatite, Ca10(PO4)6(OH)2.

questions.text: Fluoride increases the resistance of enamel to acids mainly because it forms which compound?
questions.explanation: Fluoride replaces hydroxyl ions to form fluorapatite, which is less soluble in acid.

questions.text: A patient has swollen, bleeding gums and loose teeth. His diet lacks fresh fruit and vegetables. Impaired hydroxylation of which amino acids in collagen causes these symptoms?
questions.explanation: In scurvy, lack of vitamin C impairs hydroxylation of proline and lysine, so collagen becomes unstable.

questions.text: Which type of collagen predominates in dentin and bone?
questions.explanation: Type I collagen forms the organic matrix of dentin, cementum and bone.

questions.text: Cariogenic bacteria ferment dietary sugars. Which acid is the main product that demineralizes enamel?
questions.explanation: Bacteria such as Streptococcus mutans ferment sugars mainly to lactic acid.

questions.text: Streptococcus mutans synthesizes sticky extracellular glucans from sucrose. Which enzyme catalyzes this reaction?
questions.explanation: Glucosyltransferases convert sucrose into glucans, which help bacteria adhere to the tooth surface.

questions.text: Which protein is the main component of the developing enamel matrix?
questions.explanation: Amelogenins make up about 90% of the organic matrix of developing enamel.

questions.text: A patient taking warfarin has prolonged bleeding after tooth extraction. Warfarin acts as an antagonist of which vitamin?
questions.explanation: Warfarin blocks the vitamin K-dependent carboxylation of clotting factors II, VII, IX and X.

questions.text: Children living in an area where drinking water contains 3 mg/L of a certain element have white and brown spots on their enamel. Which element causes this condition?
questions.explanation: Excessive fluoride intake during tooth development causes dental fluorosis (mottled enamel).

questions.text: Which is the main buffer system of saliva?
questions.explanation: The bicarbonate system is the most important salivary buffer, especially at high flow rates.

questions.text: A patient presents with dry skin, hyperkeratosis of the oral mucosa and night blindness. Deficiency of which vitamin is the most likely cause?
questions.explanation: Vitamin A is needed for normal epithelial differentiation and for rhodopsin in the retina.

questions.text: A child has delayed tooth eruption, enamel hypoplasia and deformed bones. Deficiency of which vitamin is the most likely cause?
questions.explanation: Rickets is caused by vitamin D deficiency and affects the mineralization of bones and teeth.

questions.text: Which microorganism is considered the main causative agent in the initiation of dental caries?
questions.explanation: Streptococcus mutans produces acid from sugars and synthesizes glucans that help it adhere to enamel.

questions.text: An infant has white curd-like plaques on the oral mucosa that can be wiped off, leaving a red surface. Which organism is the most likely cause?
questions.explanation: Oral thrush is caused by the yeast Candida albicans.

questions.text: Which Gram-negative anaerobic bacterium is strongly associated with chronic periodontitis?
questions.explanation: Porphyromonas gingivalis is a key periodontal pathogen of the "red complex".

questions.text: A patient has painful grouped vesicles on the lip that appear again during periods of stress. Which virus causes this condition?
questions.explanation: Recurrent herpes labialis is usually caused by reactivation of latent HSV-1.

questions.text: Which method is the most reliable for sterilizing dental instruments?
questions.explanation: Autoclaving (for example, 121 °C for 15–20 minutes) kills all microorganisms, including spores.

questions.text: A patient has a hard swelling of the jaw with several draining sinuses. The pus contains yellow "sulphur granules". Which organism is the most likely cause?
questions.explanation: Sulphur granules and draining sinuses are typical of cervicofacial actinomycosis.

questions.text: Dentists are vaccinated against hepatitis B. Which antigen does the vaccine contain?
questions.explanation: The recombinant hepatitis B vaccine contains the surface antigen, HBsAg.

questions.text: Why do Gram-positive bacteria retain the crystal violet stain during Gram staining?
options: They have a thick peptidoglycan layer
They have an outer membrane with lipopolysaccharide
questions.explanation: The thick peptidoglycan layer of Gram-positive bacteria traps the crystal violet–iodine complex.

questions.text: A child has fever, painful vesicles in the mouth and a rash on the palms and soles. Which virus is the most likely cause?
questions.explanation: Hand, foot and mouth disease is usually caused by Coxsackievirus A.

questions.text: Small white spots on a red background (Koplik spots) appear on the buccal mucosa before the skin rash. Which disease is this sign typical of?
questions.explanation: Koplik spots on the buccal mucosa are a pathognomonic early sign of measles.

questions.text: Which bacteria are mainly associated with the progression of carious lesions in dentin?
questions.explanation: Lactobacilli are acid-tolerant and play a major role in the progression of deep caries.

questions.text: A young man under stress has painful, bleeding gums with "punched-out" necrotic papillae and a foul smell. Which microorganisms are mainly involved?
questions.explanation: Necrotizing ulcerative gingivitis is associated with fusiform bacteria and spirochetes (fusospirochetal infection).

questions.text: Which local anaesthetic belongs to the amide group?
questions.explanation: Lidocaine is an amide; procaine, benzocaine, tetracaine and chloroprocaine are esters.

questions.text: Why is epinephrine added to local anaesthetic solutions?
options: To prolong the anaesthesia and reduce systemic absorption
To speed up the onset of anaesthesia
questions.explanation: Epinephrine causes vasoconstriction, so the anaesthetic stays at the site longer and less enters the bloodstream.

questions.text: What is the mechanism of action of local anaesthetics?
questions.explanation: Local anaesthetics block voltage-gated Na+ channels and prevent the conduction of nerve impulses.

questions.text: A 6-year-old child has grey-brown bands on the teeth. During pregnancy the mother was treated with an antibiotic. Which antibiotic is the most likely cause?
questions.explanation: Tetracyclines bind to calcium in developing teeth and cause permanent discoloration.

questions.text: Long-term use of which drug can cause gingival overgrowth (hyperplasia)?
questions.explanation: Phenytoin, nifedipine and cyclosporine are well-known causes of drug-induced gingival overgrowth.

questions.text: A few minutes after an injection, a patient develops hypotension, bronchospasm and urticaria. Which drug should be given first?
questions.explanation: Intramuscular epinephrine is the first-line treatment of anaphylactic shock.

questions.text: A patient is allergic to penicillin. Which of the following antibiotics is NOT a beta-lactam?
questions.explanation: Azithromycin is a macrolide; the other drugs are beta-lactam antibiotics.

questions.text: After several weeks of using an antiseptic mouthwash, a patient has brown stains on the teeth and altered taste. Which antiseptic is the most likely cause?
questions.explanation: Brown staining of teeth and taste disturbance are typical side effects of chlorhexidine.

questions.text: What is the main mechanism of action of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs)?
questions.explanation: NSAIDs inhibit cyclooxygenase and reduce the synthesis of prostaglandins.

questions.text: Which antidote is used in paracetamol overdose?
questions.explanation: N-acetylcysteine restores glutathione and protects the liver after paracetamol overdose.

questions.text: Which drug is a specific antagonist of benzodiazepines?
questions.explanation: Flumazenil blocks the benzodiazepine binding site of the GABA-A receptor.

questions.text: Which drug is used locally to treat oral candidiasis?
questions.explanation: Nystatin is a polyene antifungal used topically for oral thrush.

questions.text: Which antimicrobial drug is especially effective against anaerobic bacteria and protozoa?
questions.explanation: Metronidazole is active against anaerobes and protozoa and is used in necrotizing gingivitis.

questions.text: Which laboratory test is used to monitor a patient who takes warfarin before tooth extraction?
questions.explanation: Warfarin therapy is monitored with the prothrombin time expressed as INR.

questions.text: Which inflammatory cells dominate in the dental pulp at the early stage of acute pulpitis?
questions.explanation: Acute inflammation is characterized by an early infiltrate of neutrophils.

questions.text: A cyst is found at the apex of a non-vital tooth. Its epithelial lining originates from which source?
questions.explanation: A radicular (periapical) cyst develops from the epithelial rests of Malassez stimulated by inflammation.

questions.text: An X-ray shows a well-defined radiolucency around the crown of an impacted lower third molar, attached at the cementoenamel junction. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: A dentigerous (follicular) cyst surrounds the crown of an unerupted tooth and is attached at the cementoenamel junction.

questions.text: A smoker has a white patch on the buccal mucosa that cannot be scraped off and cannot be diagnosed as any other disease. What is this lesion called?
questions.explanation: Leukoplakia is a white plaque that cannot be rubbed off or characterized as another condition; it is potentially malignant.

questions.text: What is the most common malignant tumour of the oral cavity?
questions.explanation: More than 90% of oral cancers are squamous cell carcinomas.

questions.text: What is the most common benign tumour of the salivary glands?
questions.explanation: Pleomorphic adenoma is the most common salivary gland tumour and usually occurs in the parotid gland.

questions.text: Which Latin term describes loss of function as one of the cardinal signs of inflammation?
questions.explanation: The cardinal signs are rubor (redness), calor (heat), tumor (swelling), dolor (pain) and functio laesa (loss of function).

questions.text: A boy has prolonged bleeding after tooth extraction. His maternal uncle has the same problem. Deficiency of which clotting factor is the most likely cause?
questions.explanation: Haemophilia A is an X-linked deficiency of factor VIII.

questions.text: A patient has a smooth red tongue, angular cheilitis, spoon-shaped nails and microcytic hypochromic anaemia. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Microcytic hypochromic anaemia with koilonychia and angular cheilitis is typical of iron deficiency.

questions.text: A few minutes after injection of a local anaesthetic, a patient develops anaphylactic shock. Which type of hypersensitivity reaction is this?
questions.explanation: Anaphylaxis is an immediate, IgE-mediated type I hypersensitivity reaction involving mast cells.

questions.text: During healing of a tooth socket, a tissue forms that consists of new capillaries, fibroblasts and inflammatory cells. What is this tissue called?
questions.explanation: Granulation tissue is the young connective tissue rich in capillaries and fibroblasts formed during repair.

questions.text: An X-ray of the posterior mandible shows a multilocular "soap-bubble" radiolucency. A biopsy reveals a benign odontogenic epithelial tumour. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Ameloblastoma typically occurs in the posterior mandible and looks multilocular on X-ray.
